questions.prompt: Given `<ComboBox ItemsSource="{Binding Users}" DisplayMemberPath="Name" SelectedValuePath="Id" SelectedValue="{Binding SelectedUserId}" />`, what does `SelectedUserId` receive when the user picks an item?
options: The selected user's `Name`
The full `User` object
The selected user's `Id`
The index of the selected item
questions.explanation: `SelectedValuePath` tells WPF which property of the item is the "value" of the selection, so `SelectedValue` is `User.Id`. The text shown is `User.Name`, and `SelectedItem` would be the full `User` object.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson warn against handling a login form's `PasswordBox` the same way as a `TextBox` with `Text="{Binding ...}"`?
options: `PasswordBox` has no property that holds the typed value
Its `Password` property is not bindable by default, for security
`PasswordBox` only works when it is placed inside a `TabControl`
Binding a password makes the PasswordBox read-only for the user
questions.explanation: The `Password` value is not bindable by default for security reasons, and the lesson advises secure handling rather than binding the password in plain text.

questions.prompt: A ComboBox bound to `Customers` must show each customer's `Name` followed by their `Id` in gray. What should you use?
options: An `ItemTemplate` with a `DataTemplate` of two TextBlocks
`DisplayMemberPath="Name"` plus `SelectedValuePath="Id"`
`DisplayMemberPath="Name, Id"`
Set `IsEditable="True"` so the ComboBox shows both values
questions.explanation: `DisplayMemberPath` shows a single property as text. For complex UI with multiple properties, icons or formatting, use an `ItemTemplate`, as in the lesson's Name + gray Id example.

questions.prompt: Each DataGrid row needs a **Delete** button that calls a `DeleteCommand` on the ViewModel. Which column type fits?
options: `DataGridTextColumn` with `IsReadOnly="True"` and a Delete header
`DataGridCheckBoxColumn` bound to an `IsDeleted` property
A `GridViewColumn` with `DisplayMemberBinding` set to the command
`DataGridTemplateColumn` with a `CellTemplate` holding the button
questions.explanation: Use `DataGridTemplateColumn` when you need custom UI or MVVM commands inside a cell; `TextColumn`/`CheckBoxColumn` are for simple text or boolean values.

questions.prompt: Two WPF RadioButtons, Red and Blue, sit in the same StackPanel. What makes them mutually exclusive in the lesson's example?
options: Both have the same `GroupName="Color"`
They are in the same `StackPanel` with `Orientation="Horizontal"`
Each has `IsThreeState="True"`
Both bind `IsChecked` to the same property
questions.explanation: In WPF the `GroupName` property groups radio buttons; the example gives both buttons `GroupName="Color"` so only one can be selected.
